newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government's review of industry assistance has concluded that the present system is cumbersome and opaque. The review is expected to recommend the appointment of a high-level investment ambassador who is authorised to offer foreign companies financial incentives to set up business in Australia. Page 1.

Property Investment Research Pty Ltd yesterday released its inaugural compilation of Australia's biggest landlords. The group of fifty institutions, funds managers and private investors collectively control almost a third of the investment grade property in the country. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank of Australia's recent sale of 167 tonnes of its gold reserve has driven the gold market to its lowest point in 12 years. Bullion dealers are now anticipating that other central banks will follow the example, with gradual sales expected to depress the gold price further. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday indicated the Federal Government is planning a comprehensive review of work practices as part of a second wave of industrial relations reform aimed to at improving labour market flexibility and reducing unemployment. Howard said the days where outdated industrial relations practices detracted from industry competitiveness could not continue. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard called yesterday for lower interest rates. His comments were interpreted by analysts as foreshadowing an easing in official interest rates, sparking a fall in the dollar to its lowest level in 18 months. Page 1.

Senior Citibank economist Stephen Koukoulas warned yesterday that the recent plunge in the gold price could slash at least A$1 billion off Australia's export earnings over the coming year. Financial experts are also concerned that any further fall in the Australian dollar could increase inflation, negating any short-term beneficial effect on the economy. Page 1.

Negotiations between the Federal Government and the States over new financial arrangements for public hospital funding have ground to a halt over the Howard Government's refusal to guarantee it would underwrite increased demands on Medicare. Page 1.

The 1958 Shiraz vintage from the Hill of Grace vineyard in SA was sold at auction last week by Adelaide wine merchants Oddbins for A$1250 a bottle. The sale has made the 1958 Shiraz the second Australian 20th century wine ever to achieve that price range Grace vineyard owner Stephen Henschke says he is shocked but extremely pleased at the result.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday foreshadowed a possible lowering of minimum wages and unemployment benefits, citing the connection between Australia's high rates of pay and its continuing unemployment. Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has accused Howard of breaking his election promise guaranteeing living standards. Page 1.

The NSW Government was yesterday drawn into the worsening conflict between mining company Rio Tinto and its striking workers at the Hunter Valley No. 1 mine. The Government-owned FreightCorp is coming under immense pressure from Rio Tinto to find train divers who are prepared to break the picket line and transport coal mined by non-striking labour. Page 1.

A survey by AGB McNair, and commissioned by Jesuit social justice centre Uniya, has found the public exaggerates the number of boat people who arrive in Australia each year. The survey found that one-third of people believe that over 4,000 boat people seek asylum annually, in contrast to last year's actual figure of 376. Page 2.

Clothing retailer Katies Fashions (Australia) Pty Limited has been ordered to pay over $50,000 in compensation to eight migrant women who were sacked when its Surry Hills warehouse closed two years ago. Judicial Registrar David Patch ruled that Katies had acted unlawfully when it terminated the women's employment and that they were entitled to compensation. Page 2.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday placed industrial relations reform back on the political agenda by claiming that unemployment levels were related to high minimum wages. Howard also foreshadowed a widening of the work-for-the-dole scheme at the end of the year. Page 1.

Vic police yesterday confirmed they were investigating allegations made by the State Opposition that ministerial briefing notes on the ambulance contract affair had been suppressed. The Opposition have alleged that the office of former health minister Marie Tehan prevented the ambulance service from releasing documents under the Freedom of Information Act. Page 1.

The National Centre for Epidemiology and Population Health has conducted a study of 23-long-day-care centres in the ACT. The study has found that children attending child-care centres are more vulnerable to respiratory infection than those who don't because staff often fail to implement adequate hygiene standards. Page 1.

The Federal Court's judicial registrar David Patch has found that fashion retailer Katies unlawfully sacked eight women in 1995, and has ordered the company to pay over A$50,000 in compensation. The court found that Katies had discriminated against the women on the basis of their sex when its Surry Hills clothing factory was relocated to Waterloo in Sydney. Page A2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
